chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Khalid from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Ahmad from Yunus ibn 'Abdi from Yunus ibn Zabyan who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he said: 'What are the people saying regarding the souls of the Believers?' I said: 'They say they are in the craws of green birds in lamps beneath the Throne.' Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Glory be to Allah! The Believer is more prestigious to Allah than for Him to make his soul be in the craw of a bird. O Yunus! If that were the case, Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and Ali, and Fatima, and al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them), and the Proximate Angels (peace be upon them) would come to him. So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, captures him, He makes that soul into a form like its form in the world, so they eat and drink. And when the visitor comes to them, they recognize him by that very image which he had in the world.'
ai.seo_question: Where do the souls of believers reside after death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi refutes the popular folk belief that souls reside in the craws of green birds, asserting instead that the believer’s soul is too noble for such a humble abode. It establishes that in the Barzakh, the soul retains a form similar to its earthly body, enabling it to partake in sustenance and interact intimately with the Ahl al-Bayt and angels. This narrative underscores the Shia view of the continuity of identity and the elevated status of the faithful in the intermediate realm.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Ahmad, from Yunus Bin Zabyan who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What are the people saying regarding the souls of the Believers?’ So I said, ‘They are saying, ‘They happen to be in the craws of green birds in a lamp beneath the Throne’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! The Believer is more prestigious to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> than for Him<sup>azwj</sup> to Make his soul to be in a craw of a bird.
O Yunus! When it was that, there come to him Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, and Ali<sup>asws</sup>, and Syeda Fatima<sup>asws</sup>, and Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, and Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, and the Angels of Proximity. So when Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Captures him, that comes to be in a mould like his own mould used to be in the world. So they are eating and drinking, and when the comer comes over to them, they recognise him by that very image which he used to have in the world’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Khalid from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Ahmad from Yunus ibn Zabyan who has said the following:

’Once I was with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and he asked, ‘What do people say about the spirits of the believers?’ I then replied, ‘They say that they live in the craws of green birds in chandlers in paradise under the Throne.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘Allah is free of all defects. A believer is highly respected in the sight of Allah. He does not place them (the spirits of believers) in the craws of birds. O Yunus, when that (death) comes Muhammad, Ali, Fatimah, al- Hassan and al-Husayn, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, and the angels of high ranks before Allah come. When Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, causes him to die, the spirit is transferred to a form like his form in the world. They (spirits) eat and drink. When a new coming soul (spirit) joins them, they recognize him through his form which he had in the world.’”
